1.explanation:
1. lighthouse-core/gather/driver.js – This is where the driver waits for FCP (_waitForFCP) and ultimately calls Tracing.end via sendCommand with a hard 60 s timeout. To avoid hanging for the full protocol timeout, this file needs logic to cap how long we’ll wait for FCP and/or to override the timeout on Tracing.end.

2. lighthouse-core/gather/gather-runner.js – The loadPage method in GatherRunner calls driver.gotoURL with waitForFCP: true by default. To respect a new FCP threshold, this file must be updated to read a configurable maxWaitForFcp from settings and pass it through to the driver (e.g., setNextProtocolTimeout before starting FCP waiting, or turn off waitForFCP after the threshold).

3. lighthouse-core/config/constants.js – The defaultSettings object here defines maxWaitForLoad but has no maxWaitForFcp. To make the FCP threshold configurable, we must add a new defaultSettings.maxWaitForFcp (and plumb that into the config) so users can tune how long Lighthouse will hold out for FCP.

4. lighthouse-cli/cli-flags.js – The CLI flags parser only knows about --max-wait-for-load. To expose a new maxWaitForFcp configuration to end users, we need to declare and document a --max-wait-for-fcp flag here, map it to flags.maxWaitForFcp, and pass it into Lighthouse’s run path so GatherRunner and driver can consume it.
1.bug_scenario: After merging PR #6944 (“core(driver): waitForFCP when tracing”), Lighthouse’s “defaultPass” now always waits for the First-Contentful-Paint (FCP) event before calling Tracing.end. On pages that never fire FCP (or fire it after the 35 s maxWaitForLoad), tracing hangs until the 60 s protocol timeout in driver.sendCommand('Tracing.end') and errors out. The production heatmaps show the 95th percentile of loadPage-defaultPass shooting from ~20 s to ~40 s then flat-lining at 60 s when no FCP arrives. The reproducer spins up a server that never writes any paintable content and confirms that Lighthouse times out at the full 60 s.
